column1: # Chained forward application of Function-typed params — the compose family
# (design/checker-compiler-completeness-review.0.md §2.1, found 2026-08-02 as
# a live miscompile: the whole-frame replay's flat window lost the source's
# paren structure, so `f (g x)` compiled the RET count error where the
# interpreter applies both fns; noteDynFrameReplay then refused the >1-
# applicable window soundly). GRADUATED 2026-08-03 (the Stage-G single-arg
# increment): a leading Function-typed carrier applied to ONE argument —
# `(g x)` with g a param — records the same RecordDynApply event as the
# trailing spelling `(x g)` (one-arg leading and trailing collection
# converge), so the inner group collapses to an event and the outer apply
# rides the single-applicable RetReplay body tail. compose and twice moved
# to lang/spec/fn-value.tsv §8. Remaining sub-frontier here: the def-split
# spelling refuses one stage earlier on the OPEN def-bound fn-param-apply
# checker false positive (check_fn_param_apply_def_fp_test.go); graduation
# = that FP's fix. The paren-collapse records only the one-arg shape (the
# arity where the spellings' collection orders converge): a bare multi-arg
# body tail `(g x y)` rides the single-applicable whole-frame replay, while
# a CHAINED multi-arg apply `f (g x y)` keeps refusing on the two-applicable
# window (pinned in lang/go/bytecode_chained_apply_test.go).
def stage fn [[f:Function x:Integer] [Integer] [def r (f x) f r]] stage ([n:Integer] => [n add 1]) 5
